[singing] Goof boy! Goof boy! Goof boy! Goof boy! / He sits in his room when the river turns blue / Don't it stop, change a vote, play for a new / Clarity of thinking was content with himself / Tired of the whimsies, make it true.

[singing] Goof boy! Goof boy! Goof boy! [spoken] Hi, Bob. Hello. What are you doing? Waiting. Waiting for what? For everyone to join me. You're going to be waiting a long time. Oh. Why don't you have a seat? Get comfortable. You look fantastic, Bob.
[announcer voice] For those of you joining us today, this is Bob, also known as Scrotum Coat. It's a family — we just call him Scrot.
What's the matter, Scrot? Do you not like me? No, I like you. You sure? Yeah. Just sitting up here watching you, your demeanor is very depressive. I'm not used to being the focus.
I'd rather be in the shadows. You want to be behind the scenes? Yeah. You like BTS? Yes.

I've seen you around, Bob. You're wearing dashikis, looking good. Thank you. Are you happy, Bob? Yeah. In the last month you've completely uprooted your life to come work for the family. You know that's a huge commitment, and it's crazy for anybody to uproot their entire life and move somewhere for a job.
It's crazy. And I've just been watching you from afar, observing. So I'm asking you now: how do you like your experience working with the DVDASA family so far? So far, so good.
I'm learning a lot. I can't get over this feeling that you're just really sad. I'm hearing a lot of audible sighs. I'm kind of nervous. I feel weird. I don't like being alone.
But you were alone recently, weren't you? Yeah. What happened recently? I went on a trip. Where did you go? New Zealand. Why did you go to New Zealand? I've never even been to New Zealand.

I went to interview one of our biggest fans. We don't have fans, Bob. We only have family. DVDASA Allen 2? DVDASA Allen 2 is a preferred family member. Yes. So you literally — had you ever been to New Zealand before?
No. So you got on a plane by yourself and flew to New Zealand to meet one of our number-one preferred family members. Yeah. What was that experience like? That was good.
I had a good time. He was a really nice guy. Great answer, Bob. Now, previous to that — like literally three or four days before — you were part of the Poon–Steve Lee expedition to Macau.
Now, did you partake in these sexual adventures? No. I got a massage. Are you lying to me? No. No cheating? I mean, you were being watched, and you were BTS most of the time.
But there was a moment where you disappeared for quite a bit and no one knew where you went.
Oh, I went and got a massage, but it was an above-the-board, no-handjob massage. It was like the number nine. The number eight came with a handjob — I got the number nine. Oh, on the menu.
Yeah. It was with number 906? No, no. I don't know who it was. It was like an old Asian lady.

[deadpan] Oh, sorry, 907. And what was your experience being with the Poon Tang Clan and Stevie Weevy for all those days on a sex island? It was good. Those dudes are a lot of fun — super cooperative and funny. It was kind of fun to see them get to go crazy. Had you seen that much...

...male nudity in your life before? Yeah, I've seen guys naked. Where have you seen guys naked? Well, I used to run Tumblr, and some of the best Tumblrs are run by gay dudes, so sometimes you gotta see a little bit of dick to see some good posts.
Now, in that entire time, did either of those gentlemen ever try to touch you inappropriately? No. All right, Bob, well, this has been fascinating. [dry] Yeah, I'm sure it has.
Sit tight, Bob. Okay. Okay. Oh — hey, wait, I feel like lobster. Whoa. Whoa. Why do you do that to yourself? What — now you're gonna be hot and bothered. I forgot.
It is Curtis Cruz-hot tonight. I know it's gonna be hot. Maybe I should go out there now. How's it going, fam? Family? Oh, I like your socks. Thanks. Don't they look like Lobster Boy?
Oh, you got, like, lobster socks? Wait, you're spreading your toes apart? Yeah. And you put your legs apart, too? Whoa!

Hey, Critter, why don't you intro us into the show? Where's — um... I'll be sure, yeah. Who knows? He just sold out of our print, so maybe he's out getting, you know, Dom Perignon and some caviar and just partying.

[announcer voice] Welcome one, welcome all! It's DVDASA, with your co-hostesses Val, Asa, Davey, and special guest Critter Flemming! Look at that guy. Wow. I like that intro a lot. That was pretty cool. Oh, you're excited.

Yeah. What are you so excited about today? Meeting Bubblegum. So I found out that our special guest, Critter, today is — first of all, for those of you who listen to the show, you know that I've never in my life done this.
But Critter — and I won't sit here and say it's a white-person thing, because I know Asians probably do it, black people probably do it — but Critter flies to places for sporting events.
Like he'll fly to North Carolina. I think it's safe to say that's a white-person thing. No, it's a sports-fan thing. Whites, blacks, Asians, every color. You think? Definitely.

No one in my family would ever fly to a sporting event. But they don't watch sports, they don't enjoy sports. Maybe sports is a white-person thing. I mean, for Critter it's a whole experience. He goes with all his friends, they get wasted, barbecue, tailgate — it's his Comic-Con. Like, Comic-Con for me...
...is in San Diego, which is a two-hour drive for me. But if it was in New York — you've gone. Yeah, but I went to New York Comic-Con when I lived in New York.
I don't think I'd fly to New York for that, and I love comics. I love taking pictures of it, too. Yeah, I can't really think of anything that I'm such a fan of that I would...
You fly for work. Yeah, I fly for work, but I don't know that I'd fly to watch a show. But for me it's a way to recharge, get away from everything.

For three hours, four hours, you just watch sports, so you don't have to do anything. You don't think about how rough the work week was. Speaking of recharge — I know our show has a huge no-Steve-Lee, no-care following.
And as you can notice, he's not here today. And, you know, Steve, love you, bro. He's pretty much like my husband now. What do your friends call him? Your trophy husband? Harry 2.0.
He goes, hey, Dave, what are we doing tomorrow? And I go, we're doing a show. But as you guys know, I told you guys we're doing a show at 3, and I told him we're doing a show at 4.
Right. I just need a little me-time. Recharge time. As does any husband. He's a very special, special... He's a special person with very special needs.

I'll get into that later. So yeah — when I hear Critter go, hey, I'm gonna fly to North Carolina for a football game, it's a little strange. I go, okay, whatever, but then it's like, okay, I accept it, you're a sports guy. But then this week he said, hey, can I...

...get Tuesday off? I go, yeah, sure, what's going on? He's like, I'm flying back home to the Bay — which isn't that far, but still, from LA. I go, for what? For a Jay-Z and Beyoncé concert. What? You were invited. I was? Yep. So where was the invitation? Well, once Dave said he...

...didn't want to go, I figured you wouldn't want to come with me. Oh, I would have. Are you kidding? Okay, so for that — that's worth it. After this, I can text and see if there's another ticket. Really? I want to go. Okay, now I want to go.
No. You already said no. Let's all go — come on, family trip to Jay-Z and Beyoncé! How come I don't get invited? Do we get to go backstage or something? I don't even care.
No, it's just a box. I don't even care. Well, your brother's girlfriend has a nice box. What is that? You get like 20 — it's like a suite.

You're sitting in a box, eating food, and you can dance in a box without being around everybody. I've never done that. You're protected. And for those of you who don't know this about Critter, he loves live music.

Doesn't really matter what the music is. Really? You're one of those? I love live music. Well, I prefer recorded music. In my older age I've gotten into it. Really? We went to go see Guns N' Roses, and then we went straight to see that electronic music.
You just like the energy? He likes watching live performing, he likes seeing people. I didn't know you were such a huge Jay-Z fan. What's the main reason you're going — to see the music?
For Jay-Z. I've always wanted to see him and Eminem. Oh, okay. And then Beyoncé. You know, for Halloween one year I was a backup dancer. What? So I wore a leotard and high heels.
You were a backup dancer for a year? No, for Halloween. My brother and I wore leotards. Do you know his songs, Jay-Z? No. But when it comes on the radio... I'd probably know all of them.
Are you going for Jay-Z or Beyoncé? 50-50. I love Jay-Z and I love Beyoncé. They're my favorite celebrity couple, current.

Well, that's why — also because it's probably going to end soon. Oh, their marriage. We have a bet going on about that. Oh yeah, whatever happened? Was there ever — I mean, he did something inappropriate.
You know what? You guys are rock stars, just fuck. That's where you get married after your career is winding down. And they're such a good business partnership.
I don't think they should let it go to waste. All right, so you would fly to see Eminem or Jay-Z? Definitely. Where would you fly to see — what band? Britney. Really? Yeah. She's in Vegas.
I know. I want to go, but no one wants to go. I'll go with you. Okay. I would never — you would have to...

We were in Vegas, you're like, what should we do, should we go see — just 'cause if that's — you weren't joking? No, if everyone's doing it. [singing] I played with your heart. I love Britney. I would fly to see Britney. But those are close flights, San Francisco to Vegas — that's hardly even a flight.
I don't know that I would fly all the way to — I just feel like when I was younger... Vermont to see... Like Lollapalooza, or Woodstock, or any of these huge Coachella...
Burning Man. Yeah, where you can see like 40 bands. It's like, okay, that is worth a trip, because then you can hang out there. I'll go to Coachella, because it's an event.
But I wouldn't even do that now. I don't think there's one band. So you did it when you were younger. But the thing that's appealing to me about the Britney show is it's a sit-down show.
What do you mean? It's not a concert. What do you mean? Her show in Vegas is not a concert. You're not going to get up and dance to her songs and shit?
No, I get tired easily, you know? I don't like things where you have to stand for three hours, no matter who it is. I got my list of bands I would travel to see.

Okay. If they found a replacement for MCA — which there isn't — but if they were like, hey, we're going to get Snoop to do all of MCA's parts and the Beastie Boys got back together, then I would go see the Beastie Boys.
If Rage Against the Machine got back together, I'd go see them. That's it — Beastie Boys or Rage Against the Machine, I would go somewhere to see them. But even then, it would be like, maybe.

You know — Eminem, Jay-Z, Donna Lewis. Now, do you think this — Donna Lewis, that's his favorite. [singing] Near and far, always together, all of you always forever. Yeah, you sing that all the time. Do you think the audience at this Jay-Z / Beyoncé concert — is it in Oakland or San Francisco? San Fran. What do you think the percentage of blacks to whites in that audience will be?
I bet it'll be like half and half. I bet it'll be 90% white. No way. No. There are so many black people in the city. Val, have you ever traveled anywhere for anything?
No. Sports. It's gonna be at least half and half. Soccer. If anything, it's more black. I'd say half and half, or if not, more whites. It's definitely not gonna be half and half.

Or more blacks. It's gonna be more whites. Are you kidding me? Why do you say that? Because white people love Jay-Z. So do black people. Everybody loves Jay-Z. Yeah, everyone loves Jay-Z and Beyoncé, but it's more white people.
No, white people also love Jay-Z. White people just buy the CDs. Good thing we have someone going there — we'll have a nice report. Good thing we have two people potentially going there.
We're all going, I thought. Val, would you go anywhere to see Jay-Z, or...? I don't know. Who's your favorite band? Would you go anywhere to see Mariah, or...?
Yeah. Yeah, you would. I would go to a crowd to see it. Oh, see? Do you think there'd be more white people or black people at an Eminem concert? White people. Okay, you're wrong.

Because when I went to an Eminem concert — speaking from experience — look at this test! That was a test. It depends when you went — and there were more black people. Well, it depends when you went and where you went.
Okay, I went in New York City in 2000-and... Like now? Eight? No, 2007? No, like 2006. So what is that, like 10 years ago? No, it's seven. Eight years ago.
I bet you it would be more white now. Eight years ago? You're wrong. All right. I'd fly to Detroit to see him. I'd love to see him in Detroit. Ew, I wouldn't fly to Detroit for anything.
Great. Like — wait, just burst my music bubble. I'm just saying. So my friends have been asking me, and it's a good question. There's — I'm sorry, but there are pubes everywhere on this.

Yeah. Okay, so because of the brightness of this room and the amount of people with black hair — like, look, this is definitely a pube and not a head hair. [laughing] I love how you just pick it up and put it right in your hand.
There's some wrestling and some other things. Whatever, I'll keep it here, and then everyone can look at it. Well, that's why we should all be able to mark out six squares.

The six squares are yours — no one's allowed in your square area. You wish. Okay, this is my eight squares right here. Oh, sorry for interrupting you, David. Your friends have been asking. So basically — and I don't know if there's any jealousy going on — but people, I've known Critter for what, a year and a half now?
Way too long. It's been about a year and a half. No, it's longer than that. We've been doing the show for about a year and a half. Yeah, that's about when I met Critter.

Oh, really? Yeah. So — I know his memory's gone. I've known Critter for about a year and a half. Well, what's it been, two years? Yeah, at least. All right, so two years I've known Critter, and Steve Lee we've known for about half a year, six months.

So when Critter first started working for me, people were like, ha ha, what — you have a bodyguard? Yeah, he's my bodyguard. That's the original reason why you were hired — because of some stalkerish weirdos.
And they were like, no, no, no, but really, who is this guy? I go, no, he's my bodyguard, he's a spy. And then they started going, hey, you know Dan has a bodyguard?

I go, what's the big deal? I'm a guy, he guards my body — my beautiful body, this temple. And then through our work relationship, we became friends. And it became known pretty quickly that if you saw me, you'd pretty much see Critter.
Yeah. He goes where I go, I go where he goes. Now I have a new relationship with Steve Lee, so pretty much everywhere I go, he goes, because we're working on this thing together.

So is Critter no longer with you all the time? I'm like in the gutter. [laughing] Oh my god, you're like Liberace. I know I've said that a million times on a million different occasions, but you are just like Liberace. He just always swaps for the newer, younger model. Do you feel neglected?

Very. I feel like I'm just in the gutter now. What's the percentage? Critter was with me 90% of my life, and now you're with me like 60, 70% of the time. Wow. Are you sad? It's devastating. Yeah. You want to hear this conversation? Have you guys even talked about it, or you want to hear the conversation?
I heard it in the car. Between who? I'm in the backseat. Okay. Or maybe it was in the car, but this conversation happened. And Steve is sitting up there and Critter's sitting in the front.
And he looks at Steve. And it was like that movie Step Brothers. He looks at Steve and goes, hey, Steve. And Steve's like, yeah, what? Critter goes, I hate you. And Steve goes, what did I do?
And Critter goes, hey, Steve, I hate you. And Steve goes, what the fuck, man, what did I do? And he's like, Steve, I hate your fucking boots. And I was like, whoa, what's going on here?

Are you jealous, Critter? No, but I'm his fucking babysitter now. I think what happens is — so Dave will be like, we went ATVing. Okay. And the fucker lies at the ATV place and says he knows how to ride them.

So he doesn't get any directions on how to drive it. Okay. So we all just take off. And then we're way down the block and Dave goes, oh, where's Steve? And then it's like, oh, Critter, go back and get Steve.
So I go back. I'm like, Steve, do you know what you're doing? He's like, I have no idea. I'm like, okay — why did you tell the guy you knew how to fucking ride?
So I'm like, okay, stay here, I'll go get the whole group and bring everyone back, and then we're probably going to take you back in and you just ride with me. So then I go back down the block.
And these guys are there. I was like, okay, so come back down, Steve's going to wait for us. So then I come back down and he's gone. He's driven back. So I have to catch back up to him.
And I'm just — so I'm constantly — Dave's always like, you know, watch, go get him, take care of him. And so my friends are going, is your biological clock ticking?
Do you need to have a kid? Right. Because it's like having a baby. I'm a babysitter now for a 40-year-old man. Yeah. And you forget. A manny. Well, you forget, because he is 40 years —

He's older than us. He's older than both of us. Isn't that weird? Yeah. And the things you have to tell him — okay, so I'm a hypocrite when I say this, but the way he litters, and I've talked about it, it's like...

...just stop. He's so happy, just throws shit, and then — how is it different? It's just, one, Dave can afford the ticket. I still do it. The difference is he looks at you and does it like he wants you to...

...say something to him. Like, he litters in front of people while making eye contact with them, wanting them to say something. The only difference is the eye contact — you gotta make eye contact when you litter. And the spitting, you know — he spit in here, we're like, dude, it's a...

Okay. Dave's the boss, Dave can do whatever the fuck he wants to do. So Dave, what's going on then? Are you ready for a newer, younger model? Or is it that you're ready to be a dad?

...near Cold Stone. Or deserves to be fired so we can get unemployment and just retire. So we're going to Cold Stone like every night. How many nights — did we go three nights to that fucking place? It's disgusting. I love Cold Stone, it's amazing, but — there was enough room, so we just gave you a pair.

And it's an ice cream place, there's tons of kids, and — you know, I'm guilty of this also, of just not being aware sometimes of my surroundings. Uh-huh. But I think that's an Asian thing. I think that's why we're bad drivers. Well, this guy — he's talking about the most...

...sexual, disgusting things we did, and there are children sitting at the next table, and then Critter — I literally thought I saw a parent talking to a kid — you know, Steve, Steve, there's children. He's like, oh, oh, okay. So — yeah, I don't know if you're still...

...listening, Stevie Weevy, but it's a little stressful, man. I can't believe he lasted in San Diego with Dave so far, because toward the beginning Dave wanted to fire him. Fire who? Steve. Yeah, fire him. From what? He was wasting Dave's time, and then I believe I said...

...we'll wait the two months. Don't you love these conversations? Well, he turned it around. To — what's going on right now. Fire him from what? From working for me. He works for you? Yeah, I bought his time out from Sal's, from Fat Sal's.
He talked to Fat Sal, or whoever the guy there is. Sal. It's — whatever. And he goes, it's two months. Can I get my job back if I go work with this guy?
Has it not been two months? It's been exactly two months now. Today? Or like now-ish? Like this week, yeah. So what are you going to do? That's why we're having this podcast today.

What does he want to do? What do you want to do? What do you think he wants to do? Well, obviously he wants to stay. What do you want to do? We'll just continue to talk shit about him once he gets in here.
Let's talk about us. Okay. This is enough time to talk about Stevie Weevy. You've been very busy. Yes. And I know you don't like to talk about this subject, but we have to.
I can't watch the condom sex on the pornos. I can't do it. It's not that I don't like talking about it. It's that I hate that you talk shit about it.

When you watch sports, when you go see the movies, you're seeing stuntmen, you're seeing people putting themselves in danger. Well, every job — no danger, it's like...

...watching Sons of Anarchy if everyone on Sons of Anarchy was wearing a helmet. Oh, do they wear helmets? They ride bikes and shit. Yeah, but the little helmets — if they wore the big helmets covering the whole face. I mean, if you don't like it, then don't watch it, but don't...
...talk shit about it. I'm not talking shit about it. I want to get to — you're totally talking shit about it. Well, what's the problem? You just don't like seeing the condom?
I want to see the veins on the guy's dick. You can still see it through the condom, they're see-through. Unless you're like Evan Stone, where the condom barely fits over his dick.
It depends. We keep different ones on set because people like different ones. Most of the guys use Crown. What's Crown? It's just a brand called Crown.

Because I've seen guys with really big dicks not use Magnum. And Magnums are horrible. Do they sell condoms that say extra small? No, there's no fucking way. Everyone should just be an extra-extra-large.

I don't think she even has one, and then there's none. Yeah, and then you're like, this is a bummer. I don't know. I'm not talking shit, I'm just saying — when you see it, I guess it takes the fantasy away. Yeah, you're like, that's the sex that I do, that's the normal, that's what we do at home. When you watch a porno, you want to...

...see — yeah. It's the reason why Steve watches creampie: he wants there to be a risk of her getting pregnant or AIDS. Well, I don't know what to tell you, because I can't really argue that. I mean, if you don't like condom porn, then — wait, so how does your company just decide, or is there...

They asked me if I'd done this before, and yes, I did, but that was like in seventh or eighth grade. Hold on a second — that tattoo's real? Wait, what do you mean? Oh, you mean this?

So we stopped by — how did she get that? She knows the guy that runs it or something. Amazing. And so we came by. You look great, dude. I only ate noodles yesterday.

Only? And so she put all the Hello Kitty temporary tattoos on, just to try it out. It's like the most anti-diet food ever, it's all carbs. I just want to see from Steve some kind of — you see how hard Money Mark works on the music.

You see how hard I work on the art and trying to get the visual aspects of this band. In my defense, I've been memorizing the songs. I said, Steve, your only job every day is to wake up and come up with new songs, memorize the songs you've already done, and look awesome and be physically fit.
I need to get rid of this. So I said, get tattoos all over. I don't think you need to lose weight. I don't think that's the issue here. Well, it's not even about losing weight.
It's about running around stage and singing, like, four high-energy songs without getting gassed out, you know? Yeah. So maybe do some cardio? That's what I mean. Yeah, cardio, I need to do it.

Let's go over your onions, right? Yeah, yeah, yeah. So forget your whole noodle diet. No, I just — because it was by Eddie's. I like that noodle place by Eddie's. I know. Also, explain to them what the commitment is to have a good-looking body.
Yeah, help me out. It's a lifestyle. It's a complete — it's a 24/7 job. How do you stay so fit? I'm miserable. She's miserable. What do you eat? She works out every morning at 6.
Yeah, I work out every morning. She goes to Barry's Bootcamp. I watch what I eat. I only eat bad once a week. Every morning? Every single morning. Look at her body. Look at her body, dude.
Here, show them your body. I can see it right here. Look at her legs, her booty. Oh my God. You know how hard it is for an Asian girl to have a body like that?
Yeah. So you work for it, it's a commitment. When's the last time you saw an Asian girl with a body like that? It's, like, once in a blue moon. Probably here. Yeah, once in a blue moon.

You look great, buddy. Do you like the neck tattoo? Yeah, I like it a lot. Maybe you should get a real one. Like this? Yeah, but not the Hello Kitty. No. So if I get a commit and get a Monchichi or a hammer right here — or you get a tattoo?
